records.name: Controlled MBP refolding-protocol comparisons
openObligations: Purified, already synthesized clients and purified E. coli GroEL/SR1/GroES are studied in vitro. The selected data do not observe translation, cellular stress adaptation, protein damage surveillance, routing to proteasomes or organismal proteome reliability.

Adding the GroEL/GroES/ATP protocol is a combined intervention. These panels do not by themselves isolate ATP hydrolysis, individual ATPase steps, capture specificity, every component necessity or all possible active folding effects.

Activity recovery, tryptophan fluorescence, light scattering and size-exclusion elution measure different properties. None alone supplies an atomic native structure, a unique folding path or the fraction of every chain in a single native state.
All readouts and fitted rates come from one publication. No raw traces, new fit, covariance, curve digitization, independent replication or analytically-checked status is supplied.

The source interprets these conditions through aggregation prevention. Its broad passive-cage conclusion is retained as conditional, not a proof that all chaperonins are passive or that no client can experience an active conformational effect.

The DM-MBP client is mature V8G/Y283D maltose-binding protein. Tryptophan fluorescence is an environment-sensitive refolding proxy; no maltose-binding affinity, transport activity or enzymatic client assay is measured here.

The chloride-containing protocol uses 20 mM Tris-HCl pH7.5,200 mM KCl and 5 mM Mg(OAc)2 after dilution from 6 M guanidine-HCl. The chloride-deficient protocol uses 100 mM Hepes pH7.5,20 mM KOAc and 5 mM Mg(OAc)2 after dilution from 9.5 M urea. Buffer, salt concentration/anion and starting denaturant all change; chloride alone is not isolated.

Concentration dependence and light scattering support intermolecular association under the tested solution protocol. They do not identify a unique oligomer structure or prove that every fluorescence intermediate is an aggregate.

Rate equivalence in the changed solution protocol constrains a need for a faster intrinsic cage-only step for this client under those conditions. It does not prove an unchanged microscopic route or universal absence of chaperonin active effects.

records.name: Heat response of isotope-labelled E. coli DNA
openObligations: This is an externally heated lysate/DNA preparation after bacterial growth and isotope labelling, not a physiological observation of strand separation during replication.

The hybrid density band gives two separated heat-denatured density species comparable with heated heavy and light controls. Calling the inferred conserved physical units single polynucleotide strands requires the structural interpretation that this paper explicitly leaves open.

Apparent molecular-weight changes are inferred from density-band shapes and equilibrium theory. The source footnote 12 identifies an unquantified preferential CsCl/water-solvation error, so these are not unqualified absolute molecular masses or directly counted chains.
The source salmon-sperm DNA comparison behaves differently in apparent molecular-weight response; no universal heat-dissociation architecture or physiological replication mechanism is inferred.

Heating-induced separation and isotope partition are complementary contexts within one publication, not independent publications, direct sequence determination or a fully reconstituted replication machine.

openObligations: This is a synthetic DNA-origami scaffold carrying commercially supplied enzymes, not a naturally evolved protein-only multienzyme complex, living metabolic network, protein biosynthesis or a cellular-origin experiment. The scaffold DNA is supplied; its sequence-dependent assembly was not independently reconstructed.

Negatively stained TEM, dye colocalization and photobleaching report different preparations/proxies. They support source-defined loading and location, not exact atom-level interfaces, universal pair occupancy, an impermeable shell or a measured protein-protein channel.

Photobleaching copy-number estimates normalize detected Cy3 steps to labels per free enzyme and depend on labeling, detection and six-state HMM assumptions. TableS3 covers HRP, G6pDH and beta-Gal, not direct proof that every cascade cage has exactly one GOx and one HRP.

Bulk cage concentration uses A260 and an adopted extinction coefficient0.109 nM^-1cm^-1; conjugate concentrations/labeling use absorbance deconvolution and inherited coefficients. Calibration, gel-extraction losses, active-enzyme fractions and labeling are not independently reproduced.

GOx/HRP activity is a coupled ABTS absorbance readout. It depends on both enzyme steps, intermediate availability, substrate concentrations and active fractions; it is not an isolated turnover count, direct intermediate trajectory, flux control coefficient or exclusive measure of substrate transfer.

The source nominally matches enzyme/cage concentrations but paired, separately caged and uncaged preparations differ in assembly, conjugation, purification, local environment and total cage/DNA organization. No isolated geometric confinement variable or equal active-site population is proven.

Separate full cages and half-cages also increase the coupled signal. Increased activity of a co-caged pair therefore does not uniquely establish direct substrate channeling, reduced intermediate escape or a proximity-only mechanism.

Hydration-layer ordering, electrostatic stabilization and conformational-substate mechanisms are proposed interpretations. Salt/helix-density comparisons alter more than one property and do not directly measure local water structure, local pH or a unique mechanism.

The single-molecule G6pDH enzymology uses a different enzyme, surface immobilization, PMS/resazurin reporter and 10 percent PEG. It is not the same GOx/HRP bulk cascade preparation or an independent replication of its fold enhancement.

The main/SI trypsin protocol annotations differ in digestion buffer, pH, enzyme concentration and assay ABTS concentration. No new protection/aggregation or persistence claim is admitted from those conflicting annotations.

No crosstalk suppression, competing-pathway insulation, local concentration gradient, intermediate residence/retention, synchronized feedback, closed metabolic cycle, sustained living-system regulation or universal efficiency benefit is measured in the admitted contexts.

studies.finding: The source supports an enzyme-associated DNA-cage population, with proxy/calibration limits rather than universal exact pair occupancy.
limitations: This is a synthetic DNA-origami scaffold carrying commercially supplied enzymes, not a naturally evolved protein-only multienzyme complex, living metabolic network, protein biosynthesis or a cellular-origin experiment. The scaffold DNA is supplied; its sequence-dependent assembly was not independently reconstructed.

Negatively stained TEM, dye colocalization and photobleaching report different preparations/proxies. They support source-defined loading and location, not exact atom-level interfaces, universal pair occupancy, an impermeable shell or a measured protein-protein channel.

Photobleaching copy-number estimates normalize detected Cy3 steps to labels per free enzyme and depend on labeling, detection and six-state HMM assumptions. TableS3 covers HRP, G6pDH and beta-Gal, not direct proof that every cascade cage has exactly one GOx and one HRP.

Bulk cage concentration uses A260 and an adopted extinction coefficient0.109 nM^-1cm^-1; conjugate concentrations/labeling use absorbance deconvolution and inherited coefficients. Calibration, gel-extraction losses, active-enzyme fractions and labeling are not independently reproduced.

GOx/HRP activity is a coupled ABTS absorbance readout. It depends on both enzyme steps, intermediate availability, substrate concentrations and active fractions; it is not an isolated turnover count, direct intermediate trajectory, flux control coefficient or exclusive measure of substrate transfer.

The source nominally matches enzyme/cage concentrations but paired, separately caged and uncaged preparations differ in assembly, conjugation, purification, local environment and total cage/DNA organization. No isolated geometric confinement variable or equal active-site population is proven.

Separate full cages and half-cages also increase the coupled signal. Increased activity of a co-caged pair therefore does not uniquely establish direct substrate channeling, reduced intermediate escape or a proximity-only mechanism.

Hydration-layer ordering, electrostatic stabilization and conformational-substate mechanisms are proposed interpretations. Salt/helix-density comparisons alter more than one property and do not directly measure local water structure, local pH or a unique mechanism.

The single-molecule G6pDH enzymology uses a different enzyme, surface immobilization, PMS/resazurin reporter and 10 percent PEG. It is not the same GOx/HRP bulk cascade preparation or an independent replication of its fold enhancement.

The main/SI trypsin protocol annotations differ in digestion buffer, pH, enzyme concentration and assay ABTS concentration. No new protection/aggregation or persistence claim is admitted from those conflicting annotations.

No crosstalk suppression, competing-pathway insulation, local concentration gradient, intermediate residence/retention, synchronized feedback, closed metabolic cycle, sustained living-system regulation or universal efficiency benefit is measured in the admitted contexts.

The full main article and selected SI passages were read; most individual-enzyme kinetic traces and exact staple-sequence tables were not. Source ratios are approximate reported normalizations, not a new fit, digitization, data replay or independently reconstructed uncertainty.

studies.observable: Coupled ABTS absorbance at 410 nm and normalized bulk activity across cage/uncaged controls
studies.preparation: For source Figure 3 and SI Figure 12, compare nominal1 nM GOx/HRP enzyme or enzyme-DNA-cage preparations with 1 mM glucose and 2 mM ABTS in 1xTBS, pH7.5; the source bulk Methods specify1 mM MgCl2. Monitor increasing absorbance at 410 nm. The panel includes a co-caged GOx/HRP pair, a mixture of separately full-caged enzymes, a mixture of separate half-cages, free enzymes with an empty cage and free enzymes without cage. SI Figure 12 includes fresh, same-thermal-program and substrate-background controls. Figure 3 reports SD of at least three replicates. Complete base TBS salt composition and an exact common active-enzyme population are not supplied/reconstructed; source concentration/normalization conventions are retained.
